how_to_read: Each freedom carries source (native|extension|unsupported|unknown) and verified (executed_pass|executed_fail|source_only|not_run) exactly as the round brief requires. 'source_only' means the claim rests on reading pinned upstream source, NOT on running it. Nothing below is marked executed_pass for a backend, because no backend could be built or run on this host.

freedoms.question: Can an external plan control tiling and loop order?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: vendor/ONNXim_git/src/Mapping.cc:25-49 reads an optional *.mapping file of [T]/[O]/[I] loop tuples (N C M P Q S R)
freedoms.own_layer: src/schedinfra/plan/schema.py chunk model; generators choose n_tile per stage
freedoms.scope: Loop tiling only. The mapping file does not carry core placement or addresses.
freedoms.remaining_limit: No per-transfer or per-address control through this interface.

freedoms.question: Can a plan decide which core runs which tile?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Scheduler.cc:76-92 honours a tile's core_id when it is not -1, but Common.h:124 defaults core_id=-1 and nothing external sets it; only model-level target_core (Model.cc:22-23) and config partiton_map (SimulationConfig.h:80) exist
freedoms.own_layer: PlanOp.core is a first-class field and is hashed into plan identity
freedoms.scope: Would require patching tile creation, not just config.
freedoms.remaining_limit: Cannot be exercised without a build, so no execution evidence exists.

freedoms.question: Can a consumer start once its own input is visible, without waiting for the whole producer layer?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Scheduler.cc:207-209 issues a new layer only when every per-core queue is empty and count_active_layers()==0; Scheduler.cc:114-118 gates BAR tiles on launched==finished
freedoms.own_layer: Resident-pipelined generator emits per-chunk edges (292 vs 1170 edges for the naive plan at M=32)
freedoms.scope: This is the whole-layer barrier the research question depends on removing.
freedoms.remaining_limit: Removing it means changing the scheduler's issue condition, i.e. changing execution semantics, not an adapter.

freedoms.question: Can data stay in a core's scratchpad across an operator boundary?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Core.cc:36-74 flushes the scratchpad per tile (spad_id=(spad_id+1)%2 then flush); the accumulator is preserved only within one fused op (Core.cc:54-58); outputs are written back to DRAM by MOVOUT (Core.cc:364-403)
freedoms.own_layer: Plan IR models residency explicitly (5,308,416 B resident at M=32, peak 294,912-327,680 B per core)
freedoms.scope: Directly contradicts the research need. Not reachable by a thin adapter.
freedoms.remaining_limit: Would require new storage ownership semantics plus new verification.

freedoms.question: Is on-chip capacity explicit and enforced?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Sram.cc:6-10 fixes capacity at spad_size/2; overflow asserts (Sram.cc:48-50) or exits (Core.cc:338-342) rather than silently growing
freedoms.own_layer: checker.check_capacity_and_reuse enforces peak residency per core against the same 16 MiB number
freedoms.scope: Enforced, but by hard failure rather than by stalling and repricing.
freedoms.remaining_limit: A capacity violation aborts instead of producing a legal, charged alternative.

freedoms.question: Can a plan declare slot/buffer reuse and have it checked?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: AddressAllocator.h is an abstract base with a single pure virtual and is unused at runtime; double buffering is fixed at 2 (Core.cc:52-53)
freedoms.own_layer: Chunk.reuse_of plus checker rules premature_reuse / reuse_without_order_edge / slot_conflict; 6 negative tests pass
freedoms.scope: Reuse legality is checked in our layer; the backend has no matching external interface.
freedoms.remaining_limit: Not exercised against a real allocator.

freedoms.question: Can cores exchange data directly?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Simulator.cc:269-275 routes every request to a DRAM channel and every response back to a core; no core-to-core path exists
freedoms.own_layer: Not modelled. Plans that need remote data must stage through DRAM.
freedoms.scope: Staging through DRAM is allowed if explicitly charged and labelled, which the brief permits for a first version.
freedoms.remaining_limit: Distributed residency / direct core-to-core transfer cannot be studied on this backend without rewriting routing.

freedoms.question: Are dependencies and resource ordering explicit?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: per-operation tile dependencies plus the scheduler's ready handling; schedulers selected by Scheduler::create (Scheduler.cc:4-20)
freedoms.own_layer: PlanOp.deps is a partial order; checker verifies acyclicity, coverage and missing dependencies
freedoms.remaining_limit: Resource-order (as opposed to data-dependency) edges are scheduler-internal.

freedoms.question: Is the issue policy swappable through an explicit interface?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: Scheduler is a virtual base (Scheduler.h:17-23) and Scheduler::create (Scheduler.cc:4-20) selects a subclass from config; four exist: simple, time_multiplex, partition_cpu, spatial_split
freedoms.own_layer: No policy layer of our own was built, because there is no executor to plug it into
freedoms.remaining_limit: Unverified: a swap has never been executed and timed here.

freedoms.question: Do queues and credits feed back into issue?
freedoms.upstream_evidence: booksim2/ramulator2 backends report finite buffers (Interconnect.cc:111-114; Dram.cc:94-96,159-161) and Simulator.cc:157,176,183 checks is_full before pushing; with icnt_type=simple, Interconnect.cc:63-66 always returns false
freedoms.own_layer: Not modelled - our layer is deliberately timing-free
freedoms.scope: Present only with the non-simple backends; the shipped example config uses simple.
freedoms.remaining_limit: The default config this round pinned has NO backpressure.
